licences: Required to take any saltwater fish, Fla. Stat. § 379.354(1), unless a § 379.353(2) exemption applies. Spearfishing is fishing. The free resident shoreline licence, § 379.354(4)(k), covers fishing "from land or from a structure fixed to the land" only; FWC states it is not valid for taking by swimming or diving, so a diver entering from shore needs the full licence.

R. 68B-5.006(2) exempts taking lionfish while diving with a hand net, pole spear, Hawaiian sling or a lionfish-specific spear from the licence requirement. No bag or size limit. The rebreather harvest ban has an exception for lionfish only.

FREE and annual, separate from your licence, r. 68B-14.009. Required to harvest or possess these while aboard a vessel in Florida waters: almaco jack, banded rudderfish, greater and lesser amberjack; gray triggerfish; black, gag and red grouper; hogfish; mutton, red, vermilion and yellowtail snapper. A diver who enters from shore is outside the trigger. The rule was amended 1 Sep 2026 without changing this; the amendment adds a separate Atlantic For-Hire Reef Fish Registry (2026 to 2028) that owners or operators of vessels for hire must join. Whether a dive charter counts is not settled: ask FWC, 850-487-0554. The 65-and-over licence exemption does not exempt you.

Fla. Stat. § 327.331: a face mask and snorkel makes you a "diver", so freediving counts. Stay within 100 ft of the device in rivers, inlets and navigation channels and 300 ft elsewhere. A divers-down buoy may not be displayed on board a vessel.
statewide: The four buffers: r. 68B-20.003(2)

"Except as provided in Rule 68B-20.004, F.A.C., spearfishing is hereby prohibited" within 100 yards of all public bathing beaches, 100 yards of commercial or public fishing piers, 100 yards of any bridge where public fishing is legally permitted, and 100 feet of the unsubmerged portion of any jetty. Note the unit change on jetties. All four are drawn only in Palm Beach County; elsewhere only FWC-inventoried piers and the classified bridges carry a buffer. Outside Palm Beach County, assume all four apply wherever there is a beach, pier, fishing bridge or jetty.
Bridges: fishing from a bridge is lawful by default, so the buffer applies

Fla. Stat. § 316.1305 makes fishing from a bridge lawful unless FDOT investigates, finds it dangerous, and posts signs. All three steps are required. So an unposted bridge is one where fishing is legally permitted, and the 100 yd spearfishing buffer attaches. Limited-access facilities (Interstates, toll expressways) bar pedestrians, so no buffer attaches there. There is no statewide register of posted bridges.
State park waters: r. 68B-20.003(2)(e), r. 62D-2.014(9)(d)

Spearing prohibited in any water under the DEP Division of Recreation and Parks. Spear gear may only be aboard if not loaded and properly stored in a vessel passing nonstop. Does NOT reach federal parks or the National Estuarine Research Reserves. Twelve parks that adjoin water are not yet drawn (among them Navarre Beach, St. George Island, Amelia Island and Estero Bay); treat water beside any state park as closed.
Statutory closed areas: § 379.2425
John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, and the Upper Keys from the Miami-Dade/Monroe county line south through Long Key. Collier is in the statute but FWC reopened it by r. 68B-20.003(1)(a).
Florida Keys sanctuary

50 of the 76 FKNMS zones prohibit fishing entirely, spearfishing and freediving included. Carrying a speargun or pole spear in the Key Largo and Looe Key Management Areas is itself an offence unless in uninterrupted transit, 15 C.F.R. § 922.164(b)(1)(iv). 25 of the 50 are in state waters, where the 2025 Restoration Blueprint does not apply because the Governor objected; the 1997 zoning controls there, backed by Florida's own rr. 68B-6.002 and 68B-6.003(1)(b). Confirm with FKNMS, 305-809-4700.
Western Dry Rocks (Key West): seasonal closure

All fishing, spearfishing included, prohibited 1 April to 31 July in the state waters of the box, r. 68B-6.004. Transit only with spear shafts out of the gun. The rule lapses after 31 Mar 2028 unless FWC renews it.
Gear-list closures: Old Tampa Bay, Turkey and Crane Creeks

Two rules name the only gear allowed and leave spears off the list. Old Tampa Bay north of the Gandy Bridge, including every creek and bayou emptying into it: hook and line, landing or dip net, cast net, permitted crab and shrimp traps, r. 68B-25.003(2). Turkey Creek and Crane Creek (Palm Bay and Melbourne) west of their mouths: the same list without shrimp traps, r. 68B-3.009. Both are closed to spearfishing and gigging.
Volusia County: r. 68B-3.008

In Volusia inland salt waters the rule prohibits spearing any species except flounder and sheepshead, and limits the gear to a barbed spear of three prongs or fewer. The rule does not define inland salt waters; assume the whole Halifax River and Mosquito Lagoon system. A state rule, not a county ordinance.
Lobster and crabs

No spear, hook or other device that could puncture or crush a lobster, r. 68B-24.006(10); federal waters too, 50 C.F.R. § 622.404(a). No lobster at any time in the Biscayne Bay-Card Sound Spiny Lobster Sanctuary, and nobody may be in the water there from a boat carrying lobster, rr. 68B-11.001, 68B-11.003 and 68B-11.004. Pennekamp: no lobster in the two-day sport season, and in the regular season none in seven buoyed zones or on any patch reef, r. 68B-24.0065 (seven zones since 1 Jul 2026). Stone crab and blue crab may not be speared, r. 68B-13.008(1), r. 68B-45.004(1).
Monroe County canals

No discharging a speargun in any manmade canal in unincorporated Monroe County, Monroe County Code § 26-5. The City of Marathon has its own ban on firing a speargun in manmade canals, City Code § 18-27 (read 30 Sep 2026).
Local ordinances

County and city codes in 141 coastal jurisdictions were searched on 30 Sep 2026. Whole-city bans: Venice ("within or near" city waters), Cedar Key (gigs included), St. Pete Beach and Treasure Island (discharging a speargun), Bal Harbour (firing a band, spring or air spear in village waters), Lauderdale-By-The-Sea (loading a speargun), Dania Beach (spear gear on the beach or in the water) and Sunny Isles Beach (fishing by spear in the Atlantic except in designated areas). Larger structure buffers and inlet closures in Lake Worth Beach, City of Sarasota, Melbourne, Boca Raton, Pompano Beach, Marco Island and John's Pass. County park waters closed to spears in Lee, Hillsborough, Brevard and Manatee. Every local rule is treated as live. See the county notes.
National parks

Dry Tortugas NP: spearfishing prohibited park-wide, weapons broken down and stowed, 36 C.F.R. § 7.27; the Research Natural Area in the northwest 46 square miles is closed to all fishing and anchoring. Everglades NP: only a closely attended hook and line, § 7.45(d)(6). Gulf Islands National Seashore: the 2021 Superintendent's Compendium banned pole spears, spear guns, Hawaiian slings and any other projectile device in all Seashore waters, but the compendium updated 1 Sep 2026 no longer contains that provision and the park's fishing page refers spearfishing questions to FWC. Status unresolved: call the park at 850-934-2600 before spearing within one mile of Perdido Key, Fort Pickens or Santa Rosa Island. Biscayne NP: no federal regulation found bans spearfishing park-wide; state law governs. Closures researched: Legare Anchorage (no diving at all), within 100 ft of any marked channel, three harbors, and the bonefish box from 1 March to 31 May, r. 68B-7.008(5). Canaveral NS: vessels may not operate or anchor within 500 ft of the ocean shoreline.
National wildlife refuges

50 C.F.R. § 27.21 bars taking any animal on a refuge unless part 32 opens it. Opened refuges with a rule that bites: Hobe Sound (rods and reels and poles and lines only), Pinellas (fishing only from vessels around Tarpon Key), Egmont Key (two attended poles), each excluding spearing on the conservative reading; Ding Darling (no spears from Wildlife Drive); Ten Thousand Islands (no spears in the freshwater and brackish marsh); Cedar Keys (300 ft around Snake Key closed to all entry 1 March to 30 June); Merritt Island (refuge fishing permit). Passage Key and Crocodile Lake are closed to the public. Key West and Great White Heron are not opened in part 32, but FWS's own pages say fishing and diving in their waters are governed by state law. The conflict is unresolved.
Manatee zones: state No Entry and federal sanctuaries

A state No Entry zone bars "all vessels and all persons, either in vessels or swimming, diving, wading, or fishing", r. 68C-22.002(11): 21 zones in 10 counties, most at power-plant canals; Biscayne Bay west of Virginia Key is closed all year. Motorboats Prohibited zones do not bar divers. At the 11 federal sanctuaries (seven in Kings Bay, Blue Waters on the Homosassa, and the Bartow, Big Bend and Port Sutton sites in Tampa Bay) "All waterborne activities are prohibited" 15 Nov to 31 Mar, 50 C.F.R. § 17.108(a). The federal sanctuaries are not drawn.
Military areas: 33 C.F.R. part 334

Florida has 42 danger zones and restricted areas (§§ 334.500 to 334.780): Eglin, Tyndall, NAS Pensacola, NSA Panama City, KSC and Cape Canaveral, Patrick, MacDill, Mayport, Blount Island, Key West. Some are closed at all times (MacDill, the Coast Guard facilities at Mayport, Miami Beach and Destin, the Key West naval areas, NAS Pensacola, NAVSTA Mayport). Most offshore ranges close only when active. Off Dania Beach and John U. Lloyd, § 334.580 bans anchoring or attaching anything to the bottom over the reef tract at all times; the rule does not prohibit drift diving. Anywhere in Florida, no vessel or person may come within 100 yards of a large U.S. naval vessel, 33 C.F.R. § 165.2025.
Port and security zones: 33 C.F.R. part 165

Fixed zones close water to vessels and persons without Captain of the Port permission at Tampa Bay (port facilities, power plants, MacDill; no dive operations under the Sunshine Skyway main span), Port Canaveral, NAS Jacksonville, Port Everglades and the Miami Main Channel, Sector Key West, and the three Mar-a-Lago zones (the Atlantic East zone has been no-entry since 5 Sep 2025, when enforced). At the Port of Palm Beach there is no fixed port zone: the zones move with, or sit 100 yards around, passenger and hazardous-cargo vessels from the Lake Worth sea buoy in. Kennedy Space Center waters close on launch days, § 165.701.
Federal fishery areas (EEZ)

Spearfishing gear prohibited at the Ft. Pierce Inshore Reef and Key Biscayne / Artificial Reef H SMZs, 50 C.F.R. § 622.182 (the Ft. Pierce Offshore Reef SMZ rule does not ban it). Warsaw Hole spawning SMZ west of Key West: no snapper-grouper by any gear and no anchoring by fishing vessels until 2 Aug 2027, § 622.183(a)(2). Oculina experimental closed area (27°30′ to 27°53′ N, 79°56′ to 80°00′ W): no snapper-grouper, § 622.224(b)(2). North Florida, St. Lucie Hump and East Hump MPAs: no snapper-grouper, § 622.183(a)(1). Gulf: Madison-Swanson, Steamboat Lumps and the Tortugas reserves closed to all fishing; The Edges closed January to April.
Federal gear rules

In the Gulf stressed area a powerhead may not be used on reef fish, § 622.35(a); that rule does not restrict spearguns. In the South Atlantic EEZ a diver on a rebreather may not spear snapper-grouper, § 622.180(b). Highly migratory species: a speargun only for bigeye, albacore, yellowfin and skipjack tuna, from a boat with an HMS Angling or Charter/Headboat permit, § 635.21(h); never billfish, swordfish or sharks. King mackerel and Atlantic Spanish mackerel: a spear is not on the federal gear list, § 622.375(a)(1); the map treats spearing them in federal waters as not authorized. For dolphin and wahoo in Atlantic federal waters the gear rule does not exclude spears or powerheads, § 622.272(a)(1); in state waters powerhead harvest is prohibited.
Fresh water
Spearfishing is prohibited in all Florida fresh water, and spearguns may not even be possessed there.
Powerheads, bangsticks, rebreathers
No powerhead harvest in state waters, and no harvest on a rebreather except lionfish, r. 68B-20.003(7). The rule does not bar carrying a powerhead for protection.
prohibited:
Spearing prohibited by r. 68B-20.005: billfish · sturgeon · tarpon · bonefish · goliath grouper (the rule still says "Jewfish") · Nassau grouper · permit · Florida AND African pompano · all sharks · spotted eagle ray · manta and devil rays · snook · red drum · spotted seatrout · weakfish · tripletail · and the families surgeonfish, trumpetfish, angelfish and butterflyfish, porcupinefish, cornetfish, squirrelfish, trunkfish, damselfish, parrotfish, pipefish and seahorses, and puffers.

Barred by other rules: spiny lobster, r. 68B-24.006(10) · stone crab, r. 68B-13.008(1) · blue crab, r. 68B-45.004(1) · every triggerfish and filefish except gray triggerfish, ocean triggerfish and unicorn filefish: these are marine life species that may be taken only with nets and slurp guns, rr. 68B-42.001(2)(bb) and 68B-42.007 (read on a secondary copy).

Goliath: a limited hook-and-line permit harvest exists, but spearing is always prohibited, r. 68B-14.005(7); federal waters are closed to all harvest. Tripletail is barred twice: r. 68B-20.005(17) and r. 68B-49.006, which reaches federal waters. Sharks: hook and line only, r. 68B-44.006(1). Federal waters: a speargun may be used only on bigeye, albacore, yellowfin and skipjack tuna among highly migratory species, 50 C.F.R. § 635.21(h); Nassau grouper, speckled hind and warsaw grouper may not be taken in the South Atlantic EEZ, § 622.181(b).
seasons: Read this first

Values below are for 2026 and were checked on 30 Sep 2026. Seasons move by FWC executive order and federal temporary rule; check FWC and NOAA before every trip. Where a date comes from an FWC notice or news release rather than the text of an order or rule, it says so.
Gag

24 in TL. Atlantic state waters, including all of Monroe, and South Atlantic federal waters: closed since 2 Aug 2026 for the rest of 2026 (FWC EO 26-10, dates from FWC's announcement; 50 C.F.R. closure 91 FR 21389). Gulf state waters (not Monroe): open 1 to 30 Sep 2026 only, closed from 1 Oct 2026 (EO 26-26, from FWC's announcement). Gulf federal waters closed 1 Oct to 31 Dec 2026 (91 FR 29920).
Red snapper

Atlantic: state season 9 to 22 Oct 2026, 1 fish, no minimum size, hook and line, bandit gear, handline or spear only, trip declaration required; closed outside those dates (FWC EO 26-33, read from the order). Federal South Atlantic season 9 Oct to 12:01 a.m. 12 Oct 2026 (91 FR 60334); Florida exempted-fishing-permit trips run to 22 Oct. Gulf (FWC notice, secondary): open through 4 Oct; 9 to 25 Oct; 30 Oct to 1 Nov; 7 to 8, 14 to 15, 21 to 22 and 26 to 29 Nov; 5 to 6, 12 to 13, 19 to 20 and 25 to 27 Dec 2026; 1 to 4 Jan 2027. 16 in TL, 2 fish.
Hogfish

Atlantic and Keys (and Gulf waters south of 25°09′ N): open 1 May to 31 Oct only, closes 1 Nov 2026, r. 68B-14.0042 and 50 C.F.R. § 622.183(b)(4). 16 in fork, one fish. Gulf north of 25°09′ N: 14 in fork, 5 fish, open all year.
Shallow-water grouper

Atlantic and all Monroe waters: gag, black, red, scamp, yellowfin, yellowmouth, red hind, rock hind, coney and graysby closed 1 Jan to 30 Apr, r. 68B-14.0039(2). 3-grouper aggregate in the Atlantic and Monroe, 4 in the Gulf. Gulf federal waters beyond 20 fathoms closed 1 Feb to 31 Mar. From 1 Jan 2027 Gulf federal waters close to black grouper, scamp, yellowfin and yellowmouth grouper from 1 Jan to 30 Jun each year (91 FR 36545, from NOAA's bulletin).
Greater amberjack

Atlantic: 28 in fork, 1 fish, closed in April. Gulf: 34 in fork, 1 fish; the 2026 season closes 14 Oct 2026 and stays closed through 31 Aug 2027 in state waters (FWC EO 26-25, read from the order); federal Gulf waters close the same day (NOAA Fisheries Bulletin FB26-029).
Flounder
14 in TL, 5 per day; the rules do not exclude spear as gear. Closed 15 Oct to 30 Nov every year, r. 68B-48.005, in state and federal waters: in 2026, 15 Oct to 30 Nov 2026.
Snowy grouper and tilefish

Snowy grouper closed in Atlantic state waters (FWC EO 26-18, from FWC's announcement) and South Atlantic federal waters (91 FR 32906) from 7 Jun 2026 for the rest of 2026. Golden tilefish closed in South Atlantic federal waters 27 Mar to 31 Dec 2026 (91 FR 14651).
Snapper
Mutton 18 in TL. Gray 10 in state / 12 in federal waters. 10-snapper aggregate. Biscayne National Park has larger minimums and a 10-fish park aggregate, rr. 68B-7.003 and 68B-7.004.
Cobia
36 in fork. 1 per person, 2 per vessel. The rules do not exclude spear as gear in state or federal waters.
Mackerel

In state waters the rules do not exclude spear as gear. In federal waters a spear is not on the gear list for king mackerel or Atlantic Spanish mackerel, 50 C.F.R. § 622.375(a)(1); the map treats spearing them there as not authorized. For Gulf Spanish mackerel the federal gear rule does not exclude spear.
Puffer fish
Take prohibited in Martin and St. Lucie counties, r. 68B-3.007. Spearing puffers is prohibited everywhere by r. 68B-20.005.
Prohibited outright
Goliath grouper: spearing always prohibited; a hook-and-line permit harvest (1 Mar to 31 May) exists outside Martin to Miami-Dade. Nassau grouper, speckled hind and warsaw grouper: no harvest.
safety: No recompression chamber in Palm Beach County
Nearest: South Florida Center for H.O.P.E., Deerfield Beach, 954-571-9392, and Mercy Hospital, Miami, 800-662-3637 (1-800-NO-BENDS).
Narrowest shelf on the US East Coast. The Gulf Stream sets north essentially always. Live-boat drift with a competent operator on the surface.
State waters end at 3 nm on the Atlantic, 9 nm on the Gulf
Beyond that line federal rules apply: South Atlantic Council off the east coast and the Atlantic side of the Keys, Gulf Council off the west coast.
ramps: $15/day + tax or $50/yr + tax ($53.25) since 1 Oct 2025, all six county saltwater ramps. The fee fields inside FWC's dataset are stale.

In Palm Beach only Phil Foster and Burt Reynolds have 24-hour county access, 24-hr max, and the permit does not allow overnight storage. Paid overnight trailer parking: Lake Park Harbor Marina, ~$44/night.
Closed since 2 Sept 2025 for redevelopment, reopening spring 2027.
Florida has none; ramp access is entirely county or municipal. Ramps whose name contains 'PERMIT REQUIRED' need a local decal.

Palm Beach.txt: The only county with live spearfishing special acts. PBC Code App. G ch. 13 art. II (Laws of Fla. 59-1699, 59-1702): a night ban (§ 13-32), an absolute inlet ban (§ 13-33), diver-flag rules (§§ 13-36 to 13-38), a 150 ft standoff from anchored boats (§ 13-35), no sale of speared fish (§ 13-58), and two refuge areas where spearfishing on underwater breathing apparatus is prohibited (§§ 13-55, 13-56). FWC repealed three other PBC fisheries acts in r. 68B-3.038 and left these two standing. Treat as live law. Town rules (read 30 Sep 2026): Lake Worth Beach, no skin diving or spearfishing within 500 ft of the ocean, Snook Island and Bryant Park piers; Lantana, spearguns banned on the municipal beach and in its waters; Boca Raton, no diving in Boca Raton Inlet or near the Palmetto Park Road bridge; Delray Beach, no scuba from the municipal beach; Juno Beach, no loaded speargun on the beach or pier; Lake Park, no diving in the Harbor Marina. Mar-a-Lago security zones: Center and East (Atlantic) zones no-entry when enforced. South Palm Beach, Manalapan and Tequesta: no spear rule found (30 Sep 2026). Town of Palm Beach (read 30 Sep 2026): § 74-161 bars spearfishing gear on five named public beaches including Phipps and Midtown and requires guns to be carried uncocked on other Town beaches; § 74-200 sets buddy, certification, BC and flag requirements for diving off guarded beaches.

Martin.txt: No live spearfishing special act. Puffer fish take prohibited (r. 68B-3.007). Stuart, Jupiter Island and Sewall's Point codes have no spear rule (pier and bridge diving rules only). Hobe Sound NWR allows only rods and reels and poles and lines, which excludes spearing; St. Lucie Inlet Preserve State Park water is closed. Offshore, the St. Lucie Hump MPA bans snapper-grouper. Anchoring on reef or colonised hard bottom carries civil penalties, § 403.93345. Martin County code: no spear rule found in a whole-code search (30 Sep 2026).

Saint Lucie.txt: No live spearfishing special act; FWC repealed 57-1791. Puffer fish take prohibited (r. 68B-3.007). Fort Pierce: fishing, defined to include spears, banned at eight listed places including Moore's Creek and the city marina waters, and no propelling a spear in any city park area. Federal: the Ft. Pierce Inshore Reef SMZ bans spearfishing gear; the Ft. Pierce Offshore Reef SMZ rule does not ban it; the Oculina experimental closed area offshore bans snapper-grouper. Harbor Branch waterway is a manatee No Entry zone all year. Fort Pierce Inlet State Park water is closed. County code negative; Port St. Lucie and St. Lucie Village not read.

Broward.txt: No live spearfishing special act. City rules: Dania Beach bans spear gear on the beach and in the water and all diving within 100 yards of the Ocean Park pier; Lauderdale-By-The-Sea bans loading a spear gun anywhere in town and diving within 300 ft of the pier; Hallandale Beach, no spearfishing or scuba on the public beach; Pompano Beach, nothing within 100 ft of the pier and no diving in part of Hillsboro Inlet; Deerfield Beach, no snorkeling within 50 yards of the pier. Off Dania Beach and John U. Lloyd, anchoring or attaching anything to the bottom is banned at all times (33 C.F.R. § 334.580); § 334.580 does not prohibit drift diving. Port Everglades fixed security zones west of the ICW; manatee No Entry at two FPL canals. Dr. Von D. Mizell-Eula Johnson (John U. Lloyd) State Park water closed. Fort Lauderdale, Hillsboro Beach and county codes negative; Hollywood and Lighthouse Point not yet read.

Miami-Dade.txt: No live spearfishing special act. Biscayne National Park: no federal regulation found bans spearfishing park-wide; state law governs. Closures researched: Legare Anchorage (no diving), within 100 ft of any marked channel, three harbors, and the bonefish box 1 Mar to 31 May. No lobster at five park reefs or anywhere in the Biscayne Bay-Card Sound sanctuary. Key Biscayne / Artificial Reef H SMZ bans spearfishing gear. City rules: Miami Beach, no spearing from bridges, at the 29th to 33rd Street jetties or in lifeguard swim areas; Bal Harbour, no firing band, spring or air spears in village waters; Sunny Isles Beach, no fishing by spear in the Atlantic except designated areas. Manatee No Entry: Biscayne Bay west of Virginia Key all year. Bill Baggs Cape Florida and Oleta River state park water closed. Port of Miami Main Channel zone; Meloy Channel closed. County ch. 7 and City of Miami negative. The Monroe § 379.2425 closure begins at the county line.

Monroe.txt: Upper Keys (county line through Long Key) and John Pennekamp closed by § 379.2425. 50 FKNMS zones prohibit fishing; carrying a spear in the Key Largo and Looe Key Management Areas is an offence. Western Dry Rocks closed to all fishing 1 Apr to 31 Jul. Dry Tortugas NP closed to spearfishing; Tortugas reserves and Warsaw Hole closed federally. Gag closed in all Monroe state waters since 2 Aug 2026. Local: no discharging a speargun in manmade canals (§ 26-5; Marathon § 18-27); Key Colony Beach and Islamorada lobster-season diving and snorkeling bans; Layton bans taking lobster and stone crab in city waters; Key West negative. Key West naval areas and Sector Key West closed. Key West and Great White Heron refuge status is disputed. A county 300 ft lobster-season diving rule is reported but not read. Marathon: City Code § 18-27 bans using or firing a speargun on or below the surface of any manmade canal (read 30 Sep 2026).

Collier.txt: No statutory closure in force. The statute names Collier, but r. 68B-20.003(1)(a) lifts that closure. Marco Island bans swimming, snorkeling and scuba within 50 ft of any bridge. Manatee No Entry all year at Henderson Creek (Enchanting Shores) and the Faka Union basins. Ten Thousand Islands NWR bans spears only in its freshwater and brackish marsh; Everglades NP allows only hook and line. Delnor-Wiggins Pass State Park water closed. County code negative; Everglades City not checked. Naples: § 42-52, no spearfishing or gigging within 100 ft of the city pier (read 30 Sep 2026).

Lee.txt: Lee County parks ban fishing with spears at all times, and the code counts beaches, piers and "adjacent littoral waters" as park (§ 20-25); spearfishing banned at the Lynn Hall pier. Fort Myers Beach and Bonita Springs parks have the same ban. Ding Darling NWR: no spears from Wildlife Drive. The Matlacha Pass and Pine Island refuge islands are closed to the public; the water around them is a state aquatic preserve. Manatee No Entry at the FPL canals 15 Nov to 31 Mar. Cayo Costa, Gasparilla Island and Lovers Key state park water closed. Sanibel, Cape Coral, Fort Myers and Estero codes negative.

Charlotte.txt: No county or city spear rule found (county and Punta Gorda searched 30 Sep 2026); a "Spear fishing" row in the county's special-acts table was not read and is presumed a repealed act. Island Bay NWR islands are closed to the public; the surrounding water is a state aquatic preserve. Stump Pass Beach and Don Pedro Island state park water is closed.

Sarasota.txt: Venice bans spearfishing "within or near" city waters; Venice Inlet treated as closed. City of Sarasota: no spearfishing within 100 yards of any city dock, bridge, pier, wharf or jetty at a recreational area or bathing beach, none in marked channels, none within 200 ft of anglers or anchored boats. County: no diving or spearfishing in any marked navigable channel (§ 130-33(j)). Manatee No Entry: Pansy Bayou all year; Warm Mineral Springs in winter. Longboat Key negative; North Port not checked.

Manatee.txt: County beach parks: no fishing where swimming is permitted, no scuba in marked swim areas, no diving from or swimming under the three groins or any pier. Anna Maria: no spearing within 50 yards of the City Pier. Seaport Manatee security zone. Passage Key NWR is closed to the public. Holmes Beach, Bradenton Beach, Bradenton and Palmetto negative.

Pinellas.txt: St. Pete Beach and Treasure Island ban discharging a speargun citywide (Treasure Island excepts only designated areas; none found). John's Pass is closed on both sides (Treasure Island § 58-34, Madeira Beach § 78-3); no skin diving in Blind Pass. Dunedin: no spears from the marina. Caladesi Island, Honeymoon Island and Anclote Key state park water closed. Old Tampa Bay north of the Gandy Bridge is closed to spears (r. 68B-25.003). Bartow manatee sanctuary closed 15 Nov to 31 Mar. Bayboro Harbor and Weedon Island security zones; no dive operations under the Skyway main span. Pinellas NWR: fishing only from vessels. Not yet read: Pinellas County, St. Petersburg, Tarpon Springs, the Redingtons. Redington Shores: § 77-2, no speargun within 200 ft of swimmers or of a pier, dock or seawall being fished from (read 30 Sep 2026). St. Petersburg's old spear section § 7-134 was repealed in 2012.

Hillsborough.txt: County park waters: no spear or gig fishing except where designated (§ 38-25). Old Tampa Bay north of the Gandy Bridge closed to spears. MacDill AFB waters closed at all times. Port Sutton, Hooker's Point, Old Port Tampa and Big Bend security zones. Big Bend and Port Sutton manatee sanctuaries closed to all waterborne activity 15 Nov to 31 Mar, and the Big Bend discharge canal is a state No Entry zone in the same season. Egmont Key NWR allows only two attended poles, which excludes spearing. Tampa: § 16-76, no spear or harpoon in city marinas and mooring fields; § 16-41(a), no fishing off Parks department land except where designated (read 30 Sep 2026).

Pasco.txt: Pasco County's code has not been read (client not resolved); New Port Richey and Port Richey not checked. Werner-Boyce Salt Springs State Park adjoins water but is not drawn; treat its water as closed.

Hernando.txt: County code: spring-run diving rule on the Weeki Wachee and no spear guns in county parks; no saltwater closure. The county spearing special act is repealed.

Citrus.txt: Kings Bay: seven federal manatee sanctuaries closed to all waterborne activity 15 Nov to 31 Mar, and the Three Sisters area bans scuba and spear fishing in that window; Blue Waters (Homosassa) is a state and federal sanctuary. Crystal River power plant and Demory Gap channels are security zones. County and Crystal River rules cover spring headwaters only.

Levy.txt: Cedar Key bans spearing fish or other sea life, gigs included, anywhere in city limits. Cedar Keys NWR: 300 ft around Snake Key closed to all entry 1 Mar to 30 Jun. Lower Suwannee NWR has no spear rule. County and Inglis negative; Yankeetown not checked.

freshwater: The test is a taste test: there is no salinity number

Fla. Stat. § 379.101(33) defines salt water as all Florida territorial water excluding lakes, rivers, canals and other waterways "from such point or points where the fresh and salt waters commingle to such an extent as to become unpalatable because of the saline content." Note the words: the test is unpalatability alone. The phrase "and unfit for human consumption" belongs to the fresh water definition and is routinely misattached to this one. No parts-per-thousand threshold, no conductivity figure and no chloride limit exists anywhere in Florida fisheries law. Only the Steinhatchee River has a designated boundary. Other states did not solve it either: Mississippi, South Carolina and Louisiana all use geography (I-10, US 17, the Intracoastal Waterway), not salinity. Louisiana's legislature said why: salinity is "insusceptible of precise location by reason of the changes in water salinity caused by winds, tides, and rains."
"Brackish" is not a legal category
Florida recognises exactly two: fresh and salt. Brackish water is legally one or the other, decided by the palatability test.
Only one river is legally designated
The Steinhatchee: the statute declares it fresh "from its source to mouth." Every other water body is left to the commingling test, or to a commission order that appears never to have issued.
There is no official fresh/salt map

Verified negative. FWC publishes no per-river boundary list and no GIS layer. Their own guidance sidesteps it: "License requirements follow the species of fish, regardless of where they are caught." Any inland/coastal line on this map is inference, not a copied boundary.
Spearfishing in fresh water: two separate bans

R. 68B-4.012(3): no harvesting any marine species by hand or mechanically propelled spear or lance "while diving in fresh water." R. 68A-23.002(5): freshwater fish may not be taken by underwater swimming or diving, or by use of spear guns.
The possession claim is weaker than FWC states

FWC publishes "possession of spearfishing equipment in or on freshwater is also prohibited," but the closest rule text, R. 68A-23.002(9), is narrower: possession of freshwater fish together with a prohibited device. A flat possession ban exists only for Division of Recreation and Parks waters, 68B-20.003(2)(e). Treat FWC's statement as operationally binding, but it is not the rule text.
Why fresh-water rules treat bowfishing and spearfishing differently

The line is the water's surface, not the spear. R. 68B-20.002: gigging is deployed at or above the surface; spearfishing is operated by a person swimming at or below it. Fresh water permits manually operated spears, gigs, bows and crossbows from a boat or shore, for nongame fish only. Spearguns are banned regardless.
Licensing and gear rules do not reconcile

Licensing is species-based; the spearfishing ban is water-based. Holding the right licence for the species is no defence to the water-based gear ban, and vice versa. The combination licence costs about $1.50/yr more than a single, so there is no reason not to hold both.
"Inland salt waters" is never defined

The phrase appears repeatedly, including in Volusia's R. 68B-3.008, and is bounded only by reference to ocean beaches and inlet jetties. It is a subset of salt water used for county gear overlays, not a third category.
What to do when it is genuinely unclear

In a tidal river, a mangrove creek, or anywhere behind a salinity structure, the regime can move with season, drought and tide. The cautious reading is the conservative one: if you cannot establish the water is salt, treat it as fresh, because the freshwater side is where the speargun ban lives, and it is the side with criminal exposure.
